originalTitle: Australia news live: Dan Tehan sidesteps questions on Angus Taylor’s links to Icac inquiry; former Melbourne gangster sentenced to life in prison in Iraq
content: Victoria premier maintains he is a strong supporter of Airport Rail project Carroll also said his new cabinet would discuss the $34.5bn Suburban Rail Loop project, which was first announced by Daniel Andrews, championed by Jacinta Allan, and received billions of dollars from the federal government in its May budget. He would not say whether this would involve reviewing the project: I’m going to run a disciplined, proper cabinet process. But he did reiterate that he was a supporter of Airport Rail, which had stalled up until recently. Carroll said: Everyone knows there’s not a stronger supporter for airport rail … than me … airport rail will electrify the north-west – it is a gamechanger, it’s been talked about for a hundred years. And as premier, I’m very focused on airport rail. Carroll has already started work on royal commission into the construction sector The new premier also told reporters he has already asked the Department of Premier and Cabinet to start working on terms of reference for the royal commission into the construction sector he annouced yesterday. He confirmed the commission will look into the Labor government’s oversight of the Big Build, where corruption is alleged to have occurred. Carrol said: I said I want exhaustive terms of reference. No stone unturned. Whether it is top-tier contractors, subcontractors, labour hire, government, unions – these will be exhaustive terms of reference. The new Victorian premier, Ben Carroll, started his first full day in the top job at Kmart Bourke Street – a nod to his first job. He told reporters he spent eight years working at Kmart Airport West, calling them “crucible years”. But he also recalls memories “of being intimidated, of being abused, of being threatened” in the job. It’s why he’s chosen to bring forward the introduction of legislation his predecessor Jacinta Allan had already committed to: establishing workplace protection orders. Under the bill, the courts will have the power to ban or limit people’s access to workplaces when they treat frontline workers unacceptably for up to 12 months. Breaching an order could result in up to two years in prison or a fine of up to $50,000. The protections apply across all retail businesses and specified train, tram and bus operators. If passed, the scheme will begin on 29 July 2027 to allow further consultation and to ensure vulnerable people aren’t caught up. Carroll told reporters: This is a big reform, it’s been trialled in the ACT but this is going to be nation-leading and we want to make sure we get this right. NSW police seize millions in drugs, grenades and ammunition during raid A young man and woman were arrested after police seized millions of dollars worth of drugs, multiple grenades, ammunition and guns at an alleged safe house. AAP reports detectives made the find during a raid on a home in Glenfield in Sydney’s south-west on Tuesday morning. Weapons including six grenades, three semi-automatic assault rifles, four shotguns, a pistol, firearm parts and more than 1,000 rounds of ammunition were allegedly found at the scene. Six kilograms of cocaine, a kilogram each of methylamphetamine and ketamine, 15kg of cannabis, 1.1kg of heroin and 107 grams of MDMA were also allegedly discovered there. The man and woman, both 26, were arrested and charged. The man faces 27 offences and was refused bail. The woman was charged with organising/conducting/assisting drug premises and granted conditional bail. Both will appear before the courts. Significant traffic delays in Sydney this morning Sydney commuters, some frustrating news if you’re already running late for work: The M5 corridor is backed up for kilometres heading into the city, with roads closed between Beverly Hills and Mascot due to emergency work in the main tunnel. Heavy traffic is queued on the artery, with motorists advised to avoid the area and consider other routes. There’s no forecast yet as to when the motorway will reopen to citybound traffic. Search to continue for missing infant in South Australia A search will continue this morning in South Australia for a missing infant in the waters off Port MacDonnell. The baby has been missing for days after the bodies of a mother and toddler were pulled from the ocean before treacherous cliffs in the small coastal town. Police have been searching for the infant since Monday. They had to end the effort yesterday afternoon due to severe weather conditions. Dan Tehan, the shadow minister for energy, didn’t answer any questions this morning after Angus Taylor was named as a potential donor to a conservative Liberal group being investigated by the New South Wales corruption watchdog (Icac). Taylor is not accused of any wrongdoing. The opposition leader said yesterday the matter should be “allowed to run their course free from political interference or commentary. As such, the leader will not be providing a running commentary on any matters before the commission”. Tehan was asked if the Icac inquiry risked becoming a distraction for Taylor if he doesn’t clarify his relationship with the group from the hard right faction of the Liberals, known as the “Reformers”. But Tehan told RN Breakfast the focus should remain on the government in power while Icac “does its job”. He said: Let’s let Icac do its job. And in the meantime, let’s focus on the person who’s running this country. Specially designed Airbus completes marathon 24-hour flight before joining Qantas fleet A specially modified Airbus A350 plane touched down in France Tuesday after a record 24-hour test flight from Australia, ahead of it joining Qantas’s fleet next year, Agency France-Presse reports. Its 23,076-kilometre journey – across three continents and two oceans, and through two sunsets and two dawns – was one of the most-watched flights shown on the Flightradar24 tracking site. chineseContent: 维州州长坚称他是机场铁路项目的坚定支持者。卡罗尔还表示，他的新内阁将讨论价值 345 亿美元的郊区铁路环线项目，该项目最初由杰辛塔·艾伦 (Jacinta Allan) 倡导的丹尼尔·安德鲁斯 (Daniel Andrews) 宣布，并在 5 月份的预算中从联邦政府获得了数十亿美元。他不愿透露这是否会涉及对该项目的审查：我将运行一个纪律严明、适当的内阁程序。但他确实重申，他是机场铁路的支持者，该铁路直到最近才陷入停滞。卡罗尔说：“每个人都知道，没有比我更强有力的机场铁路支持者了……机场铁路将为​​西北地区带来电气化——这是一个游戏规则改变者，人们已经谈论了一百年了。”作为总理，我非常关注机场铁路。卡罗尔已经开始研究建筑业皇家委员会的工作新总理还告诉记者，他已经要求总理部和内阁开始制定他昨天宣布的建筑业皇家委员会的职权范围。他证实，该委员会将调查工党政府对大建筑的监督，据称那里发生了腐败。卡罗尔说：我说过我想要详尽的职权范围。千方百计。无论是顶级承包商、分包商、劳务雇佣、政府、工会——这些都将是详尽的职权范围。维多利亚州新任总理本·卡罗尔 (Ben Carroll) 在凯马特伯克街 (Kmart Bourke Street) 开始了他担任最高职位的第一天工作，这是对他第一份工作的致敬。他告诉记者，他在凯马特机场西工作了八年，称其为“艰难的岁月”。但他也回忆起在工作中“被恐吓、被虐待、被威胁”的记忆。这就是为什么他选择带来
